key_insight: Bayesian Dialectical Argumentation turns multi-LLM deliberation traces into per-agent reliability estimates, producing calibrated probabilities and resisting persistently unreliable agents.
engineering_relevance: This offers a zero-cost way to make council-style LLM systems safer and more trustworthy for deployment, especially where confidence calibration and adversarial robustness matter.
method: Model typed council moves as annotations from a classical annotator/reliability model.
Infer each agent’s reliability from who proposes, challenges, or concedes each answer.
Weight or invert votes using posterior reliabilities to form calibrated answer probabilities.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on binary and multi-class benchmarks, where BDA achieved the best calibration among zero-cost council aggregation methods and improved robustness against persistent adversarial coalitions.
watch_item: The approach depends on informative deliberation traces and may be harder to use if councils generate sparse or inconsistent interaction logs.
paper_title: Counting Moves, Weighing Voices: Bayesian Dialectical Argumentation for Calibrated Multi-LLM Councils under Persistent Adversaries
